settings.heading: Everything You Need to Know About Chemical Peels

settings.text: A peel is a controlled resurfacing treatment in which a clinician applies an exfoliating solution, such as glycolic, lactic, or trichloroacetic acid to dissolve dull, damaged surface cells. As that micro-layer lifts, fresh skin regenerates, collagen and elastin production surges, and active serums absorb more effectively, leaving you visibly smoother and brighter.

settings.text:
Dr Grandel Express Peel (superficial)

Instant glow; perfect before events; repeat every 2–4 weeks.

Glycolic Peel (light/medium)

Targets texture, congestion, early ageing; book a course of 4–6 sessions, each 3–4 weeks apart.

TCA Peel (medium)

Tackles pigmentation, deeper wrinkles, acne scars; most clients need 2–3 sessions spaced 6 weeks apart, with annual top-ups.

Results layer up, so while you’ll notice a dewy sheen after one visit, the real magic (faded spots, softened scars, tighter pores) peaks a few weeks after your final peel.

Hair Removal: 6–8 sessions spaced 4–6 weeks apart, then annual touch-ups.

Vascular/Pigmentation: 2–4 sessions every 4 weeks.

Maintenance: Top-ups every 6–12 months to keep results pristine.

Chemical peels refine rough texture and visibly shrink enlarged pores, creating that coveted glass-skin finish without filters. They even out stubborn pigmentation, from sun spots to post-inflammatory marks, by lifting excess melanin and encouraging uniform cell turnover. Fine lines and mild wrinkles gradually soften as collagen synthesis ramps up, giving skin a firmer, more elastic bounce.

By whisking away the dead-cell barrier, peels allow your homecare actives to penetrate far more deeply, meaning every drop of serum works harder.

settings.heading: Popular Skin Concerns Treated with Chemical Peels

settings.text:
Dullness and lack of radiance disappear as the peel’s exfoliating action unveils newer, light-reflective layers beneath. Hyperpigmentation, including sun damage and melasma patches, fades visibly because targeted acids interrupt excess pigment production.

Persistent acne and congestion calm down when oil-soluble ingredients clear blocked follicles and reduce C. acnes bacteria activity. Early fine lines around the eyes and mouth blur as resurfacing encourages fresh collagen and smoother epidermal texture.

Textural scars, from old breakouts to chickenpox marks, gradually level out thanks to repeated, controlled regeneration cycles.

settings.heading: What types of chemical peels does Deluxe Shop offer?
settings.content: Deluxe Shop offers a variety of chemical peels tailored to address different skin concerns, such as glycolic acid peels for anti-aging and salicylic acid peels for acne-prone skin. Each type is designed to meet specific needs, ensuring optimal results for every skin type.

settings.heading: How long does it take to see results from a chemical peel?
settings.content: The results from a chemical peel can often be seen immediately after the first session, with more significant improvements noticeable after multiple treatments. The skin may appear brighter, smoother, and more even-toned as the treatments progress.

settings.heading: Is there any downtime required after undergoing a chemical peel?
settings.content: The downtime after a chemical peel depends on the intensity of the peel. Light peels may have no downtime, allowing you to resume daily activities immediately, while medium to deep peels might require a few days of recovery.

settings.heading: Can I apply makeup after receiving a chemical peel?
settings.content: It is generally advised to avoid makeup immediately after a chemical peel to allow the skin to heal and breathe. Your skincare professional will provide specific aftercare instructions, including when it's safe to resume using makeup.

settings.heading: Are chemical peels painful?
settings.content: During the chemical peel process, you may experience a tingling or mild stinging sensation, but the procedure is not typically painful. Deluxe Shop uses advanced techniques to ensure the comfort of our clients throughout the treatment.
